headline: Huge optimization/addiction pass landed: performance harness and mobile optimizations are in, automation feels stronger, credits layout is fixed, Field Journal collection bonuses and prestige are live, and an uncommitted audio anti-clipping mix fix is ready for listening tomorrow.

working_tree.uncommitted_code_summary: Audio anti-clipping candidate: soft limiters/headroom on SFX and music, reduced grass-touch transient, and light music ducking only when a grass-touch SFX actually plays.
uncommitted_code_verification: cmd /c npm run build passed after the audio mix changes
untracked_non_code_to_leave_alone_unless: docs/Strategieen voor Geavanceerde Automatisering in Incrementele Games.md

tomorrow_first_moves: Run git status --short and confirm only the audio mix files plus handoff files are uncommitted.
Listen-test the current local build/dev server: background music at normal and high volume, then rapid grass clicking, crits, and combo bursts.
If the audio clipping is fixed and the click still feels satisfying, commit with message like 'Tame grass touch mix clipping', push master, and deploy to Vercel production.

If the click feels too soft, first tune TOUCH_TRANSIENT_GAIN in AudioSystem.ts upward from 0.76 toward 0.84; if music still crunches, tune GAME_MASTER_GAIN in ChiptuneMusicSystem.ts down from 0.82 toward 0.76 or duck depth down from 0.86 toward 0.82.
After the audio fix is handled, next design chunk should be prestige UX/pacing polish or dual-limiter/collection goals, not broad refactors.
do_not_forget: Performance is a first-class constraint. Use the harness and timing markers before making broad optimization claims.
The live site currently includes prestige but not the uncommitted audio anti-clipping fix.
Do not stage the unrelated research/handoff/artifact docs unless the user explicitly asks.
The user likes fast momentum and live deploys, but wants optimization kept permanently in mind for this project.
